procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine DM visit. Nothing major going on. Main thing he brings up is feeling more tired than usual for the past few months, worse late afternoon; sleeping through the night as far as he knows, works long screen days. The thirst and night urination he had in the summer are gone. No weight loss now, has actually gained a few pounds back over the holidays. Beer back to most nights since Thanksgiving, he admits.

Vitals: BP 138/86, P 76. BMI about 33.
Gen: well, obese, central distribution. No acanthosis seen on the neck today. Thyroid normal. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abd soft. No edema. Feet intact.

Labs from 12/29: fasting glucose 132, A1c 6.8 (best number we have on him).

A/P:
1. T2DM, A1c 6.8, at goal. Continue metformin 1000 BID. Credit to the summer diet changes.
2. Fatigue, nonspecific; sugars are better, not a hyperglycemia picture. Sleep hygiene and screen time discussed. Revisit at next visit if it persists.
3. HTN 138/86, continue.
4. Hyperzincemia, followed, next level with summer labs.
RTC 6 months with fasting labs.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: abdomen bigger, tired.

54M with T2DM, HTN, hyperlipidemia, obesity. Drew labs at 8 before the visit. Says his waistband has gone up a size since spring and he is dragging most afternoons. Asked directly about alcohol: back to 3-4 beers on most nights after work, plus a lot of bread, pasta and fried takeout. Denies chest pain, palpitations, dyspnea. No abdominal pain, no jaundice, no change in stool color. No leg swelling.

BP 138/86. BMI about 34.
Gen: obese, NAD. Sclerae anicteric. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen: protuberant, soft, nontender; liver edge palpable a little below the costal margin, smooth, nontender. No spleen tip. No ascites appreciated. Ext: no edema.
PHQ-2: 1.

Labs this morning: A1c 7.8 (up from 6.8). Lipids: total 220, HDL 35, LDL 130, TG 480. CMP: liver tests and kidney function normal. Zinc pending.

A/P:
1. T2DM, worse, tracks with the return to daily beer and diet. He wants to get back to what worked last summer before adding a medicine. Continue metformin.
2. Mild hepatomegaly on exam, liver tests normal. Alcohol and weight discussed plainly. He set a goal of no beer on weeknights.
3. Hypertriglyceridemia / hyperlipidemia, continue atorvastatin 40.
4. Fatigue and girth, as above.
5. HTN, continue.
6. Hyperzincemia, level pending.
RTC 6 months. Physical overdue; front desk to book.

documents.title: Zinc result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Kurt, your zinc came back at 108, in the normal range this time. Urine protein normal. The rest we went over Monday. Good luck with the no-weeknight-beer plan; let me know if you want a check-in sooner than January.

documents.title: Pharmacy refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy eRx renewal: lisinopril 20 mg and HCTZ 25 mg, 90-day. Seen 7/17. BP 138/86 at that visit. Sent with 1 refill.

documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Optometry report, dilated exam 11/28/2023. Best corrected acuity 20/20 right, 20/25 left. Pressures normal. Lens clear. Retina: no hemorrhages, exudates or neovascularization either eye; no diabetic retinopathy. Return in one year.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: DM recheck. The weeknight rule lasted about two months. No polyuria/polydipsia. No hypoglycemia. Taking all four meds, uses the pillbox now. Still tired in afternoons, no new symptoms otherwise.
O: Vitals as charted, weight up again. Heart and lungs normal. No edema. Monofilament intact.
A1c today 7.6. BMP normal, potassium normal on HCTZ.
A/P: T2DM above goal. Offered adding a second agent again, discussed options and their weight effects; he would like to wait until the physical and try once more. I will hold him to it. HTN stable. Physical booked for May with full labs.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical, 55M.

Interval: no ED visits. Raises something new: he is sleepy all day, nodding off in afternoon standups, and wakes several mornings a week with a dull headache that wears off by mid-morning. Has been going on and building over several months. No vision change, no weakness, no vomiting.

Meds unchanged: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40 qhs, HCTZ 25. NKDA. Beer still most nights.

Exam: vitals as charted. Obese, alert. Oropharynx clear. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. No leg edema. Feet: sensation intact, pulses good. Skin ok.
PHQ-2 1.

A/P:
1. Annual. Colonoscopy due 2029. Vaccines current. Labs today: CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c, UACR.
2. Daytime sleepiness and morning headaches in a man with his habitus and neck: worry is a sleep-related breathing problem. Referred to pulmonology for evaluation and a sleep study.
3. T2DM: decide on second agent once A1c back.
4. HTN, hyperlipidemia: continue.
Return after pulmonology.

documents.title: Physical results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Results from Tuesday: A1c 7.5, not where we want it but slightly better than February. Cholesterol numbers about the same as last year, triglycerides still high. Kidney, liver and urine protein normal. Blood count fine. The pulmonology office should call you within two weeks; let us know if they don't.

documents.title: RE: Physical results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: They called already, July 17 was the first opening. Thanks.

results.test: Carbon dioxide partial pressure in Arterial blood
Oxygen partial pressure in Arterial blood

reports.text: Technically adequate study, body habitus limits some windows. Left ventricle normal in size with normal wall thickness and normal systolic function, estimated ejection fraction 55-60%. No regional wall motion abnormality. Right ventricular free wall is thickened, consistent with right ventricular hypertrophy. Atria normal in size. Aortic, mitral, tricuspid and pulmonic valves structurally normal without significant stenosis or regurgitation. No pericardial effusion. Aortic root normal.
reports.conclusion: Right ventricular hypertrophy. Normal left ventricular size and function.

documents.title: Pulmonology Consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE PULMONARY AND SLEEP MEDICINE — NEW PATIENT CONSULTATION
Visit date: 07/17/2024
Referral source: primary care

The patient is a 55-year-old man with type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hypercholesterolemia and class II obesity seen for daytime sleepiness and morning headaches. He drifts off during meetings and when sitting still in the afternoon; headaches are present on waking and fade over the morning.

Medications: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg qhs, HCTZ 25 mg. No known drug allergies. Never smoker. Drinks beer most evenings. Works as a software developer.

Examination: BP 145/90, HR 88, RR 18. BMI 35. Large neck circumference. Lungs clear to auscultation. Regular heart rhythm. Pitting edema of both lower legs.

Data:
Arterial blood gas on room air: pH 7.43, PaCO2 55, PaO2 68, HCO3 32.
CBC: hemoglobin 18.5, hematocrit 55%.
Transthoracic echocardiogram today: right ventricular hypertrophy; LV normal.

Assessment: Daytime hypercapnia with a compensated pH and elevated bicarbonate in a patient with obesity, without lung disease to explain it, fits obesity hypoventilation syndrome. The elevated hemoglobin and right ventricular hypertrophy are in keeping with chronic hypoventilation.

Plan: Attended in-lab polysomnography to look for coexisting obstructive sleep apnea and guide positive airway pressure. Weight loss counseling. Advised avoiding alcohol in the evening and sedating medications. Return after the study.

Outside Pulmonary and Sleep Medicine

documents.title: Pulmonology letter
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Kurt, I received the pulmonologist's letter. The blood gas showed your carbon dioxide runs high, which is what they call obesity hypoventilation: breathing isn't fully keeping up, mostly at night. That fits the sleepiness and the morning headaches. Your red blood count is up and the heart ultrasound showed the right side of the heart working harder, both from the same problem. The sleep study they ordered is the next step, and treatment usually is a mask machine at night. Please do get the sleep study scheduled. Cutting the evening beer helps here too.

documents.title: RE: Pulmonology letter
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Wow ok, that explains a lot. Sleep lab's first slot is December, I'm on a cancellation list.

documents.title: Pharmacy refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: 90-day renewal for all four maintenance meds (metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin, HCTZ). Last visit 5/14. Approved per protocol.

documents.title: Nurse Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: 2024-25 flu and COVID given, left and right deltoid. No reactions to past doses. Observed, fine. Sleep study still December, no cancellation slot yet. DM follow-up booked 11/12.

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Make-up visit for the November no-show. Sleep study is next Tuesday. Still very sleepy in the day and the morning headaches continue. Has cut the beer to 2 most nights, he says. No chest pain. Ankles puffy by evening, unchanged.
O: Vitals as charted. Neck thick. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Trace ankle edema both sides.
A1c 7.4.
A/P:
1. T2DM, A1c 7.4, a bit lower. Continue metformin. Revisit second agent in spring.
2. OHS, followed by pulmonology. PSG 12/10. Remind him not to drive drowsy.
3. HTN, continue.
Physical in March.
